An event study: the effect period by period around adoption

Source: R/policy_evaluation.R
evstudy.Rd

Leads and lags of a policy's adoption, from a two-way fixed-effects regression on indicators of the time since adoption, with a joint test that the leads are zero (no effect before the policy, the testable part of parallel trends).

Usage

evstudy(
  data,
  unit,
  time,
  y,
  ftreat,
  leads = 4L,
  lags = 4L,
  ref = -1L,
  bin = TRUE,
  covs = NULL,
  cl = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95,
  w = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per unit and period.

unit, time, y

Column names: the unit, the period (numeric, for example a year or a month index) and the outcome.

ftreat

Column name of the period a unit is first treated (NA, 0 or Inf for a unit never treated). Treatment is taken as staying on.

leads, lags

The number of periods before and after adoption to estimate (default 4 and 4).

ref

The period left out (default -1).

bin

Bin the periods beyond the window into its end points (default TRUE).

covs

Optional column names of time-varying controls.

cl

Column name of the clusters (default the unit), or two column names for two-way clustering (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011): \(V_a + V_b - V_{ab}\), each term with the small-sample factor of the dimension with fewer clusters, and t on its \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom. A composite cluster (district by month, say) is one column made with interaction(). Fewer than ten clusters give a warning (CR1 errors are unreliable with so few; wcb is made for that case), and so does a cluster that changes within a unit.

conflvl

Confidence level of the intervals reported (default 0.95).

w

Optional column name of non-negative weights, such as population or matching weights, for weighted least squares with weighted within-means. Rows of weight 0 take no part in the fit.

Value

A data frame of class rmbl_event_study: evtm, estimate, se, lower, upper, t, p_value, with the reference period as a row of zeros; attributes pretrend (a list: F, df1, df2, p_value), vcov (of the estimated event times), n, clusters, conflvl. plot() draws it.

Details

With \(G_i\) the first treated period of unit \(i\) and \(k = t - G_i\), $$Y_{it} = \sum_{k = -L, k \ne r}^{M} \gamma_k \mathbf 1(t - G_i = k) + X_{it}'\theta + \delta_i + \mu_t + \varepsilon_{it},$$ with the reference period \(r\) (default -1, the period before adoption) left out. Times beyond the window are binned into its end points (bin = TRUE), or dropped. Units never treated have every indicator 0. The variance and degrees of freedom are those of plndid. The pre-trend test is the Wald statistic \(W = \hat\gamma_{pre}'\hat V_{pre}^{-1}\hat\gamma_{pre}\), reported as \(F = W/q\) on \(q\) and \(G - 1\) degrees of freedom.

With staggered adoption and effects that change over time, the lead and lag coefficients can mix in effects from other periods (Sun and Abraham 2021); stgatt gives the event-time effects free of that.

References

Sun L, Abraham S (2021). Estimating dynamic treatment effects in event studies with heterogeneous treatment effects. Journal of Econometrics 225(2):175-199.
doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.09.006

Applied to the effect of donations on police stops, block by quarter: Zorro Medina A, Hackett D, Green D, Vargas R (2025). Evidence of donor bias in Chicago police stops. arXiv:2504.15140 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15140).

See also

plndid, stgatt.

Examples

p <- polex()
es <- evstudy(p, "district", "month", "crmrate", "refmonth", leads = 3,
                  lags = 4)
es
#> ╭── Event study ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method              fixed-effects regression on the periods since         │
#> │                       adoption                                              │
#> │   Observations        720                                                   │
#> │   Clusters            20                                                    │
#> │   Periods             -3 to 4 since adoption                                │
#> │   Reference period    -1                                                    │
#> │   Confidence          95%                                                   │
#> │   Leads jointly zero  F(2, 19) = 1.016, p = 0.381                           │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   evtm  estimate      se  95% CI                 t  p_value                 │
#> │   ----  --------  ------  ----------------  ------  -------                 │
#> │     -3     0.086  0.3530  [-0.653, 0.824]    0.243    0.811                 │
#> │     -2     0.466  0.4552  [-0.487, 1.419]    1.024    0.319                 │
#> │     -1     0.000  0.0000  [0.000, 0.000]                                    │
#> │      0    -3.160  0.4476  [-4.097, -2.223]  -7.059  < 0.001                 │
#> │      1    -3.124  0.4189  [-4.001, -2.247]  -7.458  < 0.001                 │
#> │      2    -3.398  0.5025  [-4.450, -2.346]  -6.761  < 0.001                 │
#> │      3    -3.091  0.4993  [-4.136, -2.046]  -6.191  < 0.001                 │
#> │      4    -3.059  0.3644  [-3.822, -2.296]  -8.394  < 0.001                 │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each row is the effect that many periods from adoption, measured          │
#> │   against the reference period. The leads are jointly consistent with       │
#> │   zero, the testable part of parallel trends.                               │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
attr(es, "pretrend")$p_value
#> [1] 0.380962
plot(es)


# your own panel: eight towns over ten years, four adopting a by-law (two
# in 2019, two in 2021), with each town's population, county and income
own <- data.frame(
  town = rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"), each = 10),
  year = rep(2015:2024, times = 8)
)
i <- match(own$town, unique(own$town))
own$first <- c(2019, 2019, 2021, 2021, NA, NA, NA, NA)[i]
own$bylaw <- as.integer(!is.na(own$first) & own$year >= own$first)
own$pop <- c(12, 30, 8, 22, 15, 40, 9, 18)[i] * 1000
own$county <- rep(c("North", "South"), 4)[i]
own$income <- 50 + own$year - 2015 + cos(seq_len(80))
own$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (own$year - 2015) - 4 * own$bylaw +
  0.2 * own$income + sin(seq_len(80))
# three years either side of adoption, weighted by population
evstudy(own, "town", "year", "rate", "first", leads = 3, lags = 3,
        w = "pop")
#> ╭── Event study ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Method              fixed-effects regression on the periods since         │
#> │                       adoption                                              │
#> │   Observations        80                                                    │
#> │   Clusters            8                                                     │
#> │   Periods             -3 to 3 since adoption                                │
#> │   Reference period    -1                                                    │
#> │   Confidence          95%                                                   │
#> │   Leads jointly zero  F(2, 7) = 0.044, p = 0.957                            │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   evtm  estimate      se  95% CI                  t  p_value                │

#> │     -3    -0.327  1.1159  [-2.965, 2.312]    -0.293    0.778                │

#> │     -1     0.000  0.0000  [0.000, 0.000]                                    │
#> │      0    -4.076  0.2689  [-4.712, -3.440]  -15.158  < 0.001                │
#> │      1    -4.214  0.8271  [-6.170, -2.258]   -5.095    0.001                │
#> │      2    -4.368  1.3432  [-7.544, -1.192]   -3.252    0.014                │
#> │      3    -3.964  0.8082  [-5.875, -2.053]   -4.904    0.002                │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each row is the effect that many periods from adoption, measured          │
#> │   against the reference period. The leads are jointly consistent with       │
